title: What does the move really fix?
prompt: Lantern's maintainers list five problems with their single server. Suppose they move to AWS with a better design: posters in Amazon S3 and the database on a managed service with automated backups, but the app still on **one** EC2 instance. Select every problem that this move actually solves.
hints: Ask of each problem: is it caused by the hardware layout, or by the design and code?
A managed service changes who runs the storage and the backups. It changes nothing about how many app servers you have.
Two problems go away because the data no longer lives on one disk. The others need a different design or different habits.
explanation: Moving posters to S3 removes the full-disk problem, because S3 grows without you provisioning space. Automated backups on a managed database are stored separately from the database server, so a dead disk no longer takes the backups with it. The traffic spike is still a one-instance problem until you add a CDN, more instances or serverless pieces. Bugs in the Node.js code move with the code. And costs only fall if someone watches them; the cloud makes over-spending easier, not harder.

spike.text: The site falls over when one event goes viral.
spike.why: Not solved. The app still runs on one fixed-size instance. You fix this with caching at the edge, more capacity or serverless pieces, which section four builds.

disk.text: Poster uploads fill the server's disk.
disk.why: Solved. Amazon S3 has no disk to fill; you pay per gigabyte stored instead of provisioning space up front.

backups.text: Database backups live on the same disk as the database.
backups.why: Solved. A managed database's automated backups are kept apart from the instance, so losing the server does not lose the backups.

bugs.text: A memory leak in the Node.js app needs a restart every few days.
bugs.why: Not solved. Your code comes with you. The cloud can restart things automatically, but the leak is still yours to fix.

costs.text: Nobody knows what the hosting costs each month.
costs.why: Not solved by moving. AWS bills are detailed but only useful if you set budgets and look at them, which lesson three sets up.
